# Tobit Chapter 2 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_002_page_001.jpg

---

**2:1** In the days of Sarchedonus I returned to my house, and my wife Anna was restored to me along with my son Tobias. At the feast of Weeks — the holy feast of Pentecost — a fine dinner was prepared for me, and I sat down to eat.

**2:2** A table was set before me with an abundance of food. I said to my son Tobias: "Go, my child, and bring back whoever you can find among our kindred, any poor man who is mindful of the Lord. He shall eat with me. I will wait here for you, my child, until you return."

**2:3** Tobias went out to search for such a man among our people, but he came back and reported: "Father, one of our own people has been strangled and thrown into the marketplace; he is lying there now."

**2:4** Before I had tasted a single bite of food, I leaped up and carried him to one of the rooms until sunset.

**2:5** Then I came back, washed myself, and ate my meal in grief.

**2:6** I recalled the words of the prophet Amos, who said: "Your feasts shall be turned into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation." And I wept.

**2:7** When the sun went down, I went out, dug a grave, and buried him.

**2:8** My neighbors mocked me, saying: "Has he still not learned his lesson? Once before he had to flee on account of this very thing, and yet here he is burying the dead again."

**2:9** That same night I washed myself and went into my courtyard. I lay down to sleep against the courtyard wall with my face uncovered because of the heat.

**2:10** I did not know there were sparrows nesting in the wall above me. Their droppings fell warm into my eyes and produced white films. I went to the physicians, but they could not help me. Through all of this, Achiacharus provided for my needs until he left for Elymais.

**2:11** My wife Anna took up women's work and sent goods to those who had hired her, receiving wages in return. On the seventh of Dystros, when she cut the cloth and sent it to her employers,

**2:12** they paid her full wages and also gave her a young goat as a bonus for the household.

**2:13** When she came home, the kid began to bleat. I called to her and said: "Where did this kid come from? Is it stolen? Return it to its owners — we are not permitted to eat anything stolen."

**2:14** She said to me: "It was given to me as a gift over and above my wages." But I did not believe her and kept telling her to return it to its owners, and I flushed with shame toward her. Then she answered and said to me: "So where are your acts of mercy now? Where are your righteous deeds? Everything about you is plain for all to see!"

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

- All three translators recognized chapter 2 as a hinge chapter: Tobit's blindness results from his very righteousness, and the domestic quarrel with Anna ends the chapter on a note of bitter irony. The translation must capture both the mundane texture (a festival meal, a lost goat) and the theological stakes.
- "Acts of mercy" (eleēmosynas) reappears in v. 14 — Anna deploys Tobit's own signature virtue against him.
- "Mindful of the Lord" (v. 2) is SOPHIA's chosen rendering over "fears the Lord" or "remembers God"; it is more faithful to the Greek memnēmenon.
- "White films" preserved from EMET/LOGOS for the medical specificity of leukōmata.

---
## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

### TOB 2:1 — Feast Name
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "feast of Weeks — which is the holy Pentecost" |
| LOGOS | "feast of Weeks — the holy feast of Pentecost" |
| PNEUMA | "feast of Weeks came around — Pentecost" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. Both names are in the Sinaiticus text and should be preserved. PNEUMA's casual "came around" undersells the liturgical register.

### TOB 2:2 — Qualifier for the Guest
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "who remembers the LORD" |
| LOGOS | "who is mindful of the Lord" |
| PNEUMA | "someone who still holds God in his heart" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "Mindful of the Lord" captures the Greek memnēmenon (present participle of remember/keep in mind) without PNEUMA's expansive paraphrase. EMET's bracket-implied "the LORD" is slightly over-specific.

### TOB 2:3 — Cause of Death
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "has been strangled and thrown out" |
| LOGOS | "has been strangled and thrown into the marketplace" |
| PNEUMA | "has been murdered and thrown into the marketplace" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "Strangled" preserves the specific Greek term pepnigmenos. PNEUMA's "murdered" is interpretive; the method of death has narrative significance and should not be generalized.

### TOB 2:4 — Tobit's Response
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "before I tasted anything I leaped-up and I-took-up him to a room" |
| LOGOS | "Before I had tasted a single bite, I sprang up and carried him to one of the rooms" |
| PNEUMA | "I didn't touch my food. I jumped up right away, carried the body inside" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "Before I had tasted a single bite" conveys the immediacy well. PNEUMA's "carried the body inside" loses the specific detail of "one of the rooms" (eis tina oikēma). "Leaped up" (EMET) and "sprang up" (LOGOS) are close; SOPHIA opts for "leaped up" as more vivid.

### TOB 2:8 — Neighbors' Mockery
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "Still he is not afraid. Already before he has fled on-account-of this" |
| LOGOS | "Has he still not learned his lesson? Once before he had to flee because of this" |
| PNEUMA | "He still hasn't learned his lesson. He had to run for his life once already" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. The rhetorical question form ("Has he still not learned?") matches the Greek interrogative better than PNEUMA's flat statement. "Had to flee" is more precise than PNEUMA's "run for his life."

### TOB 2:10 — Achiacharus's Departure
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "Achiacharus was feeding me until he went into Elymais" |
| LOGOS | "Achiacharus provided for my needs until he left for Elymais" |
| PNEUMA | "my nephew Achiacharus kept us fed, until he had to leave for Elymais" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "Provided for my needs" covers a broader range than EMET's "feeding me." PNEUMA adds "had to" (not in text) and shifts from "me" to "us."

### TOB 2:11 — Anna's Employment
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "was working at-women's-tasks and was-sending [goods] to those-who-hired" |
| LOGOS | "took up women's work and earned wages by weaving" |
| PNEUMA | "took on weaving and needlework — skilled labor, contracted to local employers" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS with modification. The Greek erga gynaikeia ("women's work") is not specifically weaving; LOGOS adds "by weaving" interpretively. SOPHIA renders: "took up women's work and sent goods to those who had hired her, receiving wages in return" — following EMET's more literal structure.

### TOB 2:13 — Tobit's Accusation
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "Is-it not stolen? Give [it] back to its-owners, for it-is not permitted to-us to-eat anything stolen" |
| LOGOS | "Has it been stolen? Return it to its owners — we are not permitted to eat anything that has been stolen" |
| PNEUMA | "It's stolen, isn't it? You need to give it back. We don't keep stolen goods — we don't eat stolen goods. That's not who we are" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. Preserves the legal register ("not permitted") of the Greek. PNEUMA's "That's not who we are" is an addition that, while capturing the spirit, has no basis in the text.

### TOB 2:14 — Anna's Retort
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "And-where are your acts-of-mercy? And-where are your righteous-deeds? See, all-things are-known about-you!" |
| LOGOS | "So where are your acts of mercy now? Where are your righteous deeds? Everyone can see what kind of man you really are!" |
| PNEUMA | "Where's all that mercy of yours now? Where are your famous righteous deeds? The whole world knows what you've become!" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS with adjustments. "Acts of mercy" (eleēmosynai) must be preserved exactly as used elsewhere in Tobit — this is Anna deploying Tobit's own hallmark virtue against him. "Everyone can see what kind of man you really are!" loses the sharpness of the final Greek phrase (idou gnōsta panta peri sou). SOPHIA renders the final clause: "Everything about you is plain for all to see!"

### TOB 2:14 — Tobit's Emotional State
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "I-was-reddening because-of her" |
| LOGOS | "I flushed with anger toward her" |
| PNEUMA | "The argument turned ugly" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS with modification. The Greek ērythriazon means "to redden/blush" — indicating shame, anger, or both. "I flushed with shame toward her" captures the ambiguity better than "anger" alone. PNEUMA's "The argument turned ugly" loses Tobit's specific emotional state entirely.
